dropped.reason: Audio skip and sleep values from the reading app have no screen in this product.
The second ranker that causes H44.
The server knows session and profile, so client identity headers and session ids end. Their consent role moves to the server.
Signed token checks and the 5 minute token memory are removed by opaque tokens. S61's age_rating clause carries into server rules.
Learned genres depend on tags derived from third party captures. Series Romance, Horror and Teen pages change.
No run time call to the outside title service exists. Its genre mapping survives as data in the data repository.
The edge function route list has no meaning on a plain web server.
The characters route has no client caller, and its mass rule uses third party data.
OpenAPI lists every route, so no 501 stubs exist.

conditional.rule: Default dropped. If the owner keeps it, it becomes a single use server grant bound to the device.
conditional.reason: One owner item: 24 hour return after sign out.

changes.rule: List and rating are separate fields, each with its own version and change time. Removing from My List leaves the rating. Removing a rating leaves the list entry.
Hide is a series level fact covering all episodes. Clear history is one server operation.
No request without a kind. An old /watch/{id} link is answered once by the server: one kind found, redirect; both found, film, as today.

Server: host split and moved addresses, one table, sent as data through /v1/hello for deep links. Core: unknown address, then member and visitor redirects. In app links use final addresses, checked in CI. The API has no cookies, so the server cannot do member redirects.
Audience lists and the Kids limit leave the core. The server answers each screen call allowed or refused, and the profile answer names its home. Core maps the code to a target.
Server: size, cue count, adverts, language. Core: length against driver duration.
Server, after first frame, series only, English and active file only.
The consent check leaves the core. The server discards feedback when consent is off.
Drivers report the manifest tag. Core compares base tags. Unknown tags show the manifest's raw label. C41's full parser stays on the server.
Reason words and US wording come from the server. Core keeps timing.
Server validates id and duration. Core keeps only the rule that position above 5 s is worth sending. Episode percent comes from the title answer.
Address aliases in core routes. Saved episode in server play.

Feature values on the server. Core keeps unreachable counts as accounts required. Last good copy in the offline layer. Device key length check on the server. Country comes from the server at registration, or stays empty, because the edge trace address does not exist on a stranger's web server.
The host holds the base address.
Clock clamp replaced by age_ms; age unknown is ordered by arrival. Retries and reordered writes stay safe.
Limits stay on the server. Refresh timing is in core.
Session row and ProfileScope replace token memory and row reads.
Limits on id, season, episode and title stay. Subtitle proxy list and intro lookup end: subtitles and marks replace them.
Clauses from third party captures end: page_rhythm cap, rhythm slots, the 0.5 third party name score, depth, learned signals. S106 falls back to keywords. Stage 3 scores these pages.
Debounce and pull triggers move to the offline layer. Limits stay on the server. Age rating and blocked titles leave the settings command.
The third party list clause ends, so 1,466 of 70,911 titles (2.07 percent) leave the view and stay in the titles table. The clock arrives as input.
Schedule in the data repository. Reload rule in server index.
Third party ids become own ids.

Consent is a server fact, default off for personal rows. Until the owner answers it lives on the device session row. With consent off the server reads no personal data and discards feedback. Withdrawal deletes that profile's taste and feed events. Banner timing (1,500 ms, 7 day dismissal, hidden on the player address) stays in web. The browser's global privacy signal reaches the server as a refusal.
A refresh with no usable answer is tried again after 5, 20, 60 and then 120 s. The old 5 minute wait landed just past the server's 300 s reuse window, so one lost answer ended a good session.
Renew 120 s before expiry: C88's value holds over C7's 60 s. A 401 refreshes once and retries once; a second 401 ends the session. One refresher per device.
Expiry comes from expires_in and monotonic time, never an absolute time read against the device clock. The 120 s margin and the 400 to 403 outcome hold.
While playing, send every 30,000 ms. Also save on pause, seek, end, exit and suspend. The 5,000 ms local write ends.
Limits arrive from the server in /v1/hello and the core holds them. The client keeps no copy of its own.

Queue the position first with op id, age and boot id, send it with age_ms, and clear it on acknowledgement. Without the layer a failed send is dropped and the next heartbeat carries the newer position.
Cached screens stay fresh by the ttl in each server answer, scoped by account and profile, with one shared request per key. Failures are forgotten. The last good /v1/hello is kept.
Scope is account and profile. No sync snapshot exists, so that base ends.
Ordering uses age_ms from the command, or arrival when age is unknown. A late offline write never moves another device back. Each op answers applied, superseded or rejected.
Provider compare uses the opaque group id from the attempt, so no provider name reaches a device. The host and order rules hold.
A source on the wire is an attempt. Required: url, kind, group id, required headers, verified flag. Optional: container, codecs, height, audio, expiry. No provider name reaches a device.
POST /v1/play takes title and episode. The door knows device and profile, and the server reads title facts itself.

POST /v1/play order: eligibility, title facts, finders under a total budget, capability filter, one ranking, then attempts plus start_at, age card, audio and subtitle defaults, next episode and the count of dropped attempts. A cache hit still does no provider work.
One ranker on the server takes viewer language, original language and capability and prefers the adaptive master. Tie order is data. The client re-sort ends.
Duration and video width come from the driver's position event, and no driver decides no picture on its own. A driver that cannot report width sends has_picture unknown, and the rule stays off there.

Cues and skip buttons reach the device as time windows in view data. The host compares player time to a window, so nothing ticks across the boundary. C52's text safety and C58's visibility bounds hold.
Clients stop asking. The marks route uses the same premiere, finale and typical choice, and answers these marks when no cues exist.

POST /v1/auth/confirm records time and method on the session row. The window is 300 s and a refresh never renews it. No token claim is read and no session is replaced. Age limit changes need it. A device session has no step up power until it proves a password or code on that device.
The auth service's send email hook calls the server's mail module on the same machine. Provider is a setting, SMTP included. The refusal shape holds.
One forward migration chain replaces the setup file, and CI compares a fresh install to a migrated one. server/deploy/auth-init makes roles, schema, generated secrets, OTP length 8 and expiry 600.
The deny by default model holds. ProfileScope, minted only by the door, replaces row level rules.

Unrated titles use the model profile where present and are refused below 18 otherwise. A title with no profile fails closed on sample data. The hero path's allowance at 12 and 15 ends. Owner default until the owner answers.
The client copy ends. Kids Reality follows the server rule in S67. Owner default until the owner answers.
Two named profiles over one deny table: fetch guard (5 hops, no cookies) and provider client (10 redirects, cookies).
Embed templates return only to a client that declares embeds.
On TV browsers with no secure store, tokens are short lived and revocable.
Off by default. With no engine value no figure shows, unless the owner keeps the invented figure.
Manifest equality replaces the one sided 95 percent test.
A hash per file in one manifest replaces the size and time stamp, so a copy keeps working and a wrong file swap is refused.
Only done answers enter the 6 hour cache. Failures stay 5 minutes.
The disabled provider rule holds. The one provider that needs the insecure client does not move, and neither does that client.

changes.rule: A bad file keeps the last good value. A missing file gives the default.

The API is bearer only with no cookies, so CORS answers * and a null Origin stays safe. Origin lists and the canonical origin end. The profile header ends, because the active profile sits on the session. Rate limits hold.
Title head data comes from the server's own titles table. No call to the outside title service happens at run time.
Lasting refusal codes reach the server as the trailer refused command, and the server's trailer choice skips them. Codes 2 and 5 stay unrecorded. The kept counts hold.
Settings come from environment files per host under a name the operator sets. No file name carries a brand.

gates.rule: The build fails if core gains std, async, a clock or IO. Web must import the crate.
Six exports carry bytes. The contract depends on serde only.
Old client replay: a dated version range with server transforms, never exact equality.
Built new per device family. The ABI matrix includes armv7, and a test covers the container filter.
Resolve, pin, check each hop, deny table per range, byte cap while reading, and a lint against other HTTP clients.
No vendor runtime, run time config, no owner value in any file.
Fuel, memory cap, blocking pool, total budget with partial answer, panic per provider, verified flag, real not found, one match rule, byte caps, title facts from the server.
A declared capability, off by default, off in store builds, sandboxed, covered by a CSP generator test, with a timeout and a way out, last in order.

No snapshot or list diff exists. Per field versions, one id delete, series hide, per op answer, elapsed age with boot id, one writer per session, flush on suspend, sign out and profile switch, and two device fixtures with the layer on and off.
A bare id does not parse.
A 30 s heartbeat plus saves on pause, seek, background, close and end.
Pages read library and durable taste, and dislike counts.
Active profile on the session, fail closed, TierVisible and Visible with one fixture set across lists, art, title and play, PIN and step up on the server, blocked titles enforced, unrated rule fixed.
An opaque cursor with an HTTP test.
Start deadline, classified errors, teardown before open, position kept, ended and season rollover.
Server only. The finder returns facts, headers are required in the attempt, and CORS facts are scoped to the web class.
A recovery route, a set main route, and UI tests.
Build, publish, prove. Ready shows age, and an alarm fires.
Hashes, model, dimensions and keys in one manifest. A mix is refused, no trust switch exists, the pipeline is public, and a sidecar table lists every file.
Errors counted, semaphore, deadline, shed, one vector copy, sized maps, a bad optional file ignored, text index required.
Build and data hash in ready.
Handlers in a library. Tests gate merge and release.
Local token check, 429 kept apart from 401, meter before outside calls.
Swap with health and rollback, kept releases, outside check, client reports, one migration path, tested restore, phone path included.
Wasm, JS and CSS scans. No Component Model.
Black box suites with public result tables, written with the first release.
Exact toolchain, --locked everywhere, tools in a lock file, actions by commit, and a CI step that builds twice and compares bytes.
A licence lint on every file, every capture derived file absent, and a CI scan.
No title data client in apps.

new.rule: Diagnostics page: network check, playback specification and speed test. The speed test address is a setting, and the test is off when unset.
Help tools stay in web and act on this browser: diagnostics, data, profiles, language, cookies, refresh. Help and legal text comes from the server. Clearing history is the server's one operation.
Signed out title data: GET /v1/public/titles/{kind}/{id} answers under the visitor tier, cacheable, with no profile.
Network and company logos join the data pulls. The networks column holds names only today.
Subtitles in system picture in picture and wireless display stay a written gap: the app draws its own line, which those modes cannot show. No design solved it.
The games route becomes the games screen behind the existing feature switch, default off.
Original audio gets a screen: GET /v1/screens/language.

Device sign in runs in the core. Action::DeviceSignIn asks for a code, and polling runs on next_wake_ms, one interval from each answer. slow_down adds 5 s. expired_token, or a code past its life, fetches a new code with no press. access_denied waits for a press. A network failure keeps polling with no notice. A 503 unsupported sets off. A session from any path ends it. The device code reaches no view and is not kept.
/activate is a place that takes an account and no profile, even where visitors may browse. RouteTarget.code carries its code to the screen. A visitor keeps the whole address through sign in as next.

A device code takes one answer. Approve and deny refuse a code already answered with 403 error.device_decided, in one conditional write, so of two answers at once one lands. A poll writes only its own time, so it cannot wipe an answer.

The profile chooser's titles: GET /v1/profiles/gate answers at most three titles for the whole account, never above the most open tier among its profiles (the Kids tier when every profile is a Kids profile), with no news, talk, soap, reality or documentary, each with a logo, a poster and a backdrop. Each carries its line as facts, never words: coming with a day within 30 days, seasons_coming with the day a new season starts, ranked with its place and kind in today's Top 10, or none. The choice turns each day.
Notifications and Remind Me: GET /v1/notifications, GET /v1/notifications/count, POST /v1/notifications/read, Command::Remind, Change::Remind.
Feed builder for notifications: last 30 and next 30 days, coming titles, reminder live, new seasons and episodes, new arrivals, deduped and capped.
Phone notifications page, bell count badge, Remind Me toggle, and local delivery without vendor push.

POST /v1/auth/signup answers done and carries no tokens. A free address and a taken one hear the same words, pay for the same password hash and wait on the same one letter: a free address gets its account and a sign in code, the holder of a taken one is told that someone tried to use it. The device signs in afterwards with the password it chose.
